intro: Krabi is a paradise of limestone cliffs, white-sand beaches, and crystal-clear Andaman islands — great for both sea adventures and inland nature. This guide picks out the tours and tickets you can pre-book: 4 Islands, Railay, Phi Phi, Hong Island, and nature-lovers' classics like Emerald Pool and hot springs. It tells you who each suits, the price, when to go, and links you straight to Klook to book.
quickAnswerHtml: Krabi attractions you can pre-book: 4 Islands tour (Poda Island, Chicken Island, Tup Island, and Phra Nang Cave Beach — a sandbar connects the islands at low tide), Phi Phi tour (Maya Bay, crystal water), Hong Island (beautiful lagoon, kayaking), and inland nature at Emerald Pool + hot springs + Tiger Cave Temple. Most offer a choice of speedboat or longtail boat, priced around 900–2,000 THB per person (national park fees paid separately on-site). Clearest water is Nov–Apr. Railay is accessible by boat only.

blocks.html: Krabi stands out for its limestone karsts rising from the sea and its fine white sand. There are plenty of ways to enjoy it — island hopping and snorkelling, heading to Railay for rock climbing and beach time, or going inland for the Emerald Pool and Tiger Cave Temple. Almost every tour can be booked in advance and usually includes pick-up and drop-off. This guide helps you match the right experience to your style and time.

blocks.text: How to Make the Most of Krabi

blocks.html: With 3 days you can split it simply: a sea day (4 Islands tour or Phi Phi / Hong Island), a nature day (Emerald Pool + hot springs + Tiger Cave Temple, which requires climbing about 1,237 steps to the summit), and a Railay day (gorgeous beach and rock-climbing cliffs, accessible only by longtail boat from Ao Nang). For comparing other island tours see the island-hopping guide, or if scuba is your thing check the diving guide. The Andaman's clearest water runs Nov–Apr.

blocks.title: Tips for getting the most out of Krabi

items.title: Take the morning departure
items.text: Calmer seas and fewer crowds — especially at Maya Bay and popular snorkelling spots.

items.title: Budget for park entry fees
items.text: Island tours carry national park fees paid on-site, separate from the tour price (~400 THB per person for non-Thais).

items.title: Railay is boat-only
items.text: There's no road to Railay. Catch a longtail boat from Ao Nang — it only takes a few minutes, but allow extra time if boats are full.

items.title: Reef-safe sunscreen
items.text: Use reef-friendly sunscreen. Bring a hat and a UV-protection rash guard for snorkelling.

faq.q: What are the unmissable attractions in Krabi?
faq.a: The 4 Islands tour (Poda / Chicken / Tup islands + Phra Nang Cave Beach), Railay Beach (gorgeous shore and rock-climbing cliffs), and Hong Island (lagoon kayaking) are the sea highlights. For inland nature, don't miss the Emerald Pool, hot springs, and Tiger Cave Temple.

faq.q: How much do Krabi tours cost?
faq.a: Roughly 900–2,000 THB per person depending on the tour and boat type (speedboat vs longtail). Pick-up, drop-off, and lunch are usually included. Island tours carry an additional national park fee paid on-site (~400 THB per person for non-Thais).

faq.q: How do you get to Railay?
faq.a: Railay has no road access — you travel by longtail boat from Ao Nang (or from Krabi town). The ride is short. It's a favourite for its beach scenery and rock climbing, and is sometimes included in 4 Islands tour packages.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Krabi?
faq.a: The Andaman coast has its clearest water and calmest seas from Nov to Apr — ideal for island tours. During monsoon season (May–Oct) waves pick up and some boat tours may be cancelled, though the Emerald Pool and other inland attractions are open year-round.

faq.q: What are the Emerald Pool and Tiger Cave Temple like?
faq.a: The Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot) is a translucent green freshwater pool in the jungle where you can swim. Nearby is a natural hot spring for soaking. Tiger Cave Temple has a viewpoint at the summit reached by climbing roughly 1,237 steps — great for active travellers and nature enthusiasts.
